Looking at this problem, I need to evaluate:
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \left( \int_1^{1+\frac{1}{n}} \left\{ [(x+1)\ln x +1] e^{x (e^x \ln x +1)} + n \right\} \, dx \right)^n$$

## Step 1: Find the antiderivative of the complicated term

I examine $e^{x(e^x \ln x + 1)}$. Note that $e^{x(e^x \ln x + 1)} = e^{x e^x \ln x + x} = e^x \cdot e^{x e^x \ln x}$.

Let $g(x) = x \, e^x \ln x$. Computing:
$$g'(x) = e^x \ln x + x\, e^x \ln x + x\, e^x \cdot \tfrac{1}{x} = e^x\!\left[(1+x)\ln x + 1\right]$$

Therefore:
$$\frac{d}{dx}e^{g(x)} = g'(x)\,e^{g(x)} = e^x\!\left[(1+x)\ln x + 1\right] e^{x e^x \ln x} = \left[(x+1)\ln x + 1\right] e^{x(e^x \ln x + 1)}$$

So the antiderivative of $[(x+1)\ln x + 1]\,e^{x(e^x \ln x + 1)}$ is $\boxed{e^{x\, e^x \ln x}}$.

## Step 2: Evaluate the integral

$$I_n = \int_1^{1+1/n}\!\left\{[(x+1)\ln x+1]\,e^{x(e^x\ln x+1)}+n\right\}dx = \Big[e^{x\,e^x\ln x}+nx\Big]_1^{1+1/n}$$

At $x = 1+1/n$: $e^{(1+1/n)\,e^{1+1/n}\,\ln(1+1/n)} + n(1+1/n) = e^{(1+1/n)\,e^{1+1/n}\,\ln(1+1/n)} + n+1$

At $x = 1$: $e^{1\cdot e\cdot\ln 1} + n\cdot 1 = e^0 + n = 1 + n$

Subtracting:
$$I_n = e^{(1+1/n)\,e^{1+1/n}\,\ln(1+1/n)} + (n+1) - (1+n) = e^{(1+1/n)\,e^{1+1/n}\,\ln(1+1/n)}$$

## Step 3: Compute the limit

$$(I_n)^n = \exp\!\Big(n\,(1+\tfrac{1}{n})\,e^{1+1/n}\,\ln(1+\tfrac{1}{n})\Big)$$

Let $t = 1/n \to 0^+$. The exponent becomes:
$$(1+t)\,e^{1+t}\cdot\frac{\ln(1+t)}{t}$$

As $t \to 0^+$:
- $(1+t) \to 1$
- $e^{1+t} \to e$
- $\frac{\ln(1+t)}{t} \to 1$

So the exponent $\to 1 \cdot e \cdot 1 = e$.

## Result

$$\lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\int_1^{1+1/n}\left\{[(x+1)\ln x+1]\,e^{x(e^x\ln x+1)}+n\right\}dx\right)^n = e^e$$
